title.en: Causal Machine Learning and Policy Evaluation

tagline: Estimate who benefits from a programme with machine learning, evaluate allocation rules offline before using them, and choose a rule under a budget and a fairness constraint that ends in the trial that would confirm it
description: Participants use machine learning to estimate who benefits from a programme and to choose the rule that allocates it. On a fictional employment agency's synthetic coaching pilot and logged caseworker decisions, they estimate average effects by double machine learning, estimate and validate heterogeneous effects, evaluate allocation rules offline and learn a rule under a budget and a fairness constraint. Every rule ends with the trial that would confirm it.
audience: Specialists. Data scientists who have completed the level 300 core or can show equivalent work: a defended analysis with a validated model or a causal estimate that they can explain.
prerequisites: DS-302 Online Experiments and A/B Testing
DS-303 Causal Inference from Observational Data
Estimates propensity scores and reads balance diagnostics
Trains and cross-validates machine learning models in Python

Setup: a laptop CPU with uv, or Google Colab. Nothing calls or downloads a model. Three hours of pre-work on potential outcomes and propensity scores (labs/P0_prework_refresher.ipynb) with its entry quiz before Day 1; see labs/README.md.

outcomes.text: Implement double machine learning with cross-fitting for an average effect and compare it with regression adjustment, given logged data with 60 confounders and a known effect
outcomes.evidence: an estimate table with intervals and each method's bias

outcomes.text: Build conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimators by three methods and validate them on held-out randomised data, given the randomised coaching pilot
outcomes.evidence: calibration and ranking checks per estimator and a justified choice

outcomes.text: Evaluate allocation rules offline with inverse propensity and augmented estimators and diagnose untrustworthy estimates, given logged decisions with recorded propensities and poor overlap in places
outcomes.evidence: a value table with intervals, overlap diagnostics and effective sample sizes

outcomes.text: Design an allocation rule under a budget and a fairness constraint and compare it with treat-all, risk targeting and current practice, given unit-level effect estimates and one place per five job seekers
outcomes.evidence: gains and outcomes by region, gender and disability status, with the attributes the rule may use

outcomes.text: Review a heterogeneous-effect claim for overfitting, unstable subgroups and reuse of data for discovery and evaluation, given an analysis with seeded faults
outcomes.evidence: a review memo naming each fault and its effect

outcomes.text: Design a confirmatory trial for a learned rule, powered for the comparison with current practice, given the capstone rule and its offline value
outcomes.evidence: a protocol with randomisation unit, primary metric, sample size and stopping rule

case_study.name: Fursa Employment Agency
case_study.summary: Fursa Employment Agency (وكالة فرصة للتوظيف) is a fictional public employment agency with six fictional regions and twelve offices, and all of its data are synthetic, generated with a fixed seed and carrying known true effects: a randomised coaching pilot of 6,000 job seekers and 40,000 logged caseworker decisions with 60 confounders and the offer probability the allocation tool recorded. Next year it has one coaching place for every five job seekers. Planted problems (a risk score that ranks the hopeless and the fine first, groups almost never offered coaching, nonlinear confounding through administrative history, a later extract without the motivation note, an office whose recorded probabilities are wrong, a rule resting on a few heavy weights, an analyst's subgroup claim with four seeded faults, remote seekers left behind by an unconstrained rule) are each found by a named lab. Participants work as Ohood Al-Saqabi, a senior data scientist answering Wijdan Al-Hazzaa, the director of employment services, with Duhaim Al-Thumairi, head of caseworkers, and Shuruq Al-Obaikan, the data protection officer.

format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

days.title: Capstone: a policy evaluation and its defence
days.subtitle: One brief, one constrained rule, its offline value, a subgroup audit and a trial plan, defended in 15 minutes

capstone.summary: A policy evaluation for one of three synthetic briefs (coaching places, energy-saving visits, food-safety inspections): effects, a constrained rule, its offline value, a subgroup audit and a trial plan, in a public repository whose README reports measured results; 15-minute defence
capstone.submission: A link to a public GitHub repository whose README reports measured results for one of the three briefs in labs/capstone/: the estimand, the average effect with its overlap, CATE estimates validated on the held-out randomised split, a rule under the brief's budget and a fairness constraint with the attributes it may use, its offline value with intervals and diagnostics against treat-all, risk or need targeting and current practice, an audit by the brief's groups and a confirmatory trial plan, with notebooks that rerun from the raw data with a fixed seed, the commit history, the run log and a verification note on assisted steps. Then a 15-minute live defence in which the assessor changes the budget or the fairness constraint and the participant predicts the change in policy value before re-running.
